correctness.rationale: PASS: The exact rational tails of the fixed normalized Wang–Zhong ellipse yield p',q' and factorizations p'−q'∝P4/[(z−1936)²(100z−121)²], p'+q'∝P6/[(z−1936)²(5z+242)²(100z−121)²]. The direct frozen exact arithmetic verifier was read, and an independent from-scratch rational polynomial checker run from the source constants verified both rational factorizations. Cayley-transformed P4 has positive quartic Hurwitz coefficients satisfying both strict determinants, so p'−q' has no zero in the closed unit disk. P6(−r) increases on [0,1] and has its sole radial root rho in (0.961916078016035,0.961916078016036). For |z|=rho, form T(r,x)=Re(P6(z) conj(P4(z)(5z+242)²)) with x=cos θ. The divided difference [T(r,x)−T(r,−1)]/(x+1) has six strictly positive Bernstein coefficients throughout the exact rational root bracket. Independent exact rational reconstruction verified positivity of all six lower margins, with lower margins scaled by 10^49 approximately [4.282,3.820,3.319,2.777,2.193,1.566]. Thus Re[(p'+q')/(p'−q')]>0 inside |z|<rho and is nonnegative with the sole first-circle zero z=−rho. Since J=|p'−q'|² Re[(p'+q')/(p'−q')], local sense-preserving univalence holds precisely on that maximal centered open disk. Lewy's theorem blocks all larger centered disks; the result does not assert global injectivity.
